title: The Red Hat
pages: Cat found a red hat under the old oak tree.
‘It is much too big,’ said Dog. Cat wore it anyway.
WHOOSH! A gust lifted the hat into the sky.
Cat and Dog chased it over the hill and past the pond.
The hat landed on six tiny ducks.
‘At last—a shady roof!’ quacked Mama Duck.
Cat looked at the happy ducks. ‘You can keep it.’
On the walk home, Dog found Cat a little blue cap. It fit just right.

title: Cat on a Map
pages: One morning, Cat found a map under his breakfast bowl.
A red dotted path curled through the garden.
Cat hopped across three stones and crept under the hedge.
A sleepy Dog guarded the gate. Cat gave him a gentle pat.
At the tallest sunflower, the red dots stopped. An X marked the dirt.
Cat dug and found a tiny box. Inside was a note: LOOK UP!
A basket of strawberries swung above his head.
Cat shared every last berry with Dog. Treasure tastes better together.

title: Dog in the Sun
pages: Dog loved the warm sun. He stretched out on the grass.
Soon his nose was hot. His ears were hot. Even his tail was hot.
He squeezed under Cat’s little chair. ‘No room,’ said Cat.
He tried the birdbath. SPLASH! ‘No dogs,’ chirped the birds.
So Dog dug a cool, shady hole beneath the tree.
His paws found water, and the hole became a puddle.
Dog rolled in the mud until only his wagging tail was clean.
When the sun dried him, Dog had spots. Cat laughed, and Dog did too.

title: The Big Bug
pages: Bug wanted to march in the garden parade.
But Bug was so big that the flower bridge bent under her feet.
‘I will stay home,’ sighed Bug.
Cat tied two strong leaves together and made a little boat.
Bug floated beside the parade, waving to every bee and beetle.
Then rain rushed down, and the tiny marchers lost their way.
Bug lifted them onto her broad red back and carried them home.
‘Three cheers for Big Bug!’ they cried. Bug stood very tall.

title: Pig Can Dig
pages: Pig loved to dig. She dug by the gate, under the bench, and between the carrots.
‘Please stop!’ said Cat. Every path was full of holes.
Pig tried to sit still. Her nose twitched. Something smelled wonderful.
She dug one last, careful hole and found a small clay pot.
Inside was a single brown seed and a note: ADD SUN AND RAIN.
Pig planted the seed and filled in every other hole.
Soon a red flower opened, then ten, then a hundred.
Cat smiled. ‘You can dig our garden any day.’

title: A Nap for Dad
pages: Dad Bear yawned. ‘I need one small nap.’
Little Bear brought him three pillows, two blankets, and one cup of tea.
‘Now I need a story,’ said Dad.
Little Bear read about a dragon who could not sleep.
Dad closed his eyes, but Little Bear whispered, ‘Are you asleep yet?’
No answer. Dad was finally snoring.
Little Bear tucked him in, climbed beside him, and listened.
Soon Little Bear snored too. Dad opened one eye and smiled. Best nap ever.
